How Palisade works

Redirect the energy and let natural processes help.

Each Palisade unit combines a high-strength synthetic panel with a fabricated steel attachment assembly fitted over pipe pilings driven into the riverbed. The units are positioned with varying locations, angles, lengths and permeability so the reach functions as one coordinated system.

The system reduces velocity within the near-bank control zone and redirects stronger flow toward the channel. Where sediment conditions allow, that lower-energy zone can encourage accretion, vegetation and renewed bank stability.

  1. Evaluate the River

    Document channel geometry, flow behavior, bank movement, sediment conditions and nearby assets.

  2. Model the Response

    Determine how the river may respond and whether a coordinated river-training system fits the conditions.

  3. Engineer and Install

    Set piling and panel locations, angles, lengths and permeability, then install the system across the designed reach.

  4. Observe the Control Zone

    Monitor how flow, sediment and vegetation respond as the protected bank begins to stabilize.

Why river training matters

The solution addresses movement, not just damage.

Moves Velocity Away

The system targets the energy driving bank migration rather than only covering the eroded surface.

Adapts to the River

Variable spacing and permeability allow the system to be tuned for different flow and sediment conditions.

Protects Long Reaches

Multiple structures work together as a system instead of relying on one isolated point of protection.

Supports Habitat Recovery

Reduced near-bank velocity and sediment deposition can support riparian and aquatic habitat.

The goal is not an online diagnosis

It is a better first conversation.
